main_body: A roofed structure: a blue-grey tiled canopy on two wooden posts, with a grey stone basin holding water below
top_band: Basin: light rim at row 30 (#b9b9bc), water surface rows 31-35, then the grey front face from row 36. Roof: ridge highlight at rows 1-2, then the tiled slope (two tile tiers, rows 4-14).
evidence: The basin reads as a 3/4 piece. Row 30 is a light rim, rows 31-34 are a blue water surface, row 35 is a light front-lip line, and rows 36-42 are the grey front face. The roof is a large tiled slope with a ridge highlight and a dark underside at rows 15-17, much like the reference roofed well. Its slope is shown as a surface, not a 1-2px cap. The posts are vertical supports. This is borderline for the roof, since its top band is only about 2 rows, but the overall structure is not a flat elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has 23 distinct colours and a median of 9 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. All of its dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), where the references' are 1% and 33%, so the outline is a near-black sticker line instead of a tinted material tone. The roof has some tile shading, but the basin front is a flat grey block of about 6 rows in one tone with no stone texture. The posts are plain flat ochre. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the references.
